web-preflight release

Checks a site you own before you ship it, without pretending a status code is a finding. A 200 on /.env that matches the app shell is catch-all routing, a blanket 403 is an unanswered question, and a check that never ran becomes INCONCLUSIVE — never a pass.

4 verdicts · 19 fixed paths · 9 behavioral tests · ~215 lines · 0 API keys

crash-test decisions

Crash-tests a decision before you build it. Four fixed roles draft the same task in separate contexts and attack each other's drafts anonymously; the chair merges what survived on evidence, not votes, keeps a dissent log for what it could not settle, and grounds the winner's claims about your files against the source before adopting them.

4 roles · ~9 calls · 1 opt-in Operator seat · 2 modes · 0 API keys

findable discovery

Sets up discovery for a GitHub repo, skill, plugin or MCP server so it gets found by what it does, not only by its name. It audits where you rank today, works out the queries strangers type, then drafts the About text, topics, README opening, release notes, site page and directory plan — real numbers only, and nothing public changes without your go-ahead.

8 workflow steps · 10 kit sections · 4 reference guides · 1 listing validator · 0 API keys

pre-ship-performance-audit performance

Audits and fixes a web app's real-world speed before launch: four read-only subagents sweep twenty known slow-downs across images, bundles, database queries and servers, then the same mobile Lighthouse protocol, three runs per page, proves each fix before and after. Never removes a feature for a score, never invents a baseline, and asks before touching dependencies, the database or the deploy region.
